Specification: This specification models an inner serial memory/register interface that tracks per-process sequences of issued operations, their responses, and a partial order over operation identifiers. It distinguishes read and write requests, records the source write that supplies a read value, and constrains the evolving order relation so that the completed history is serializable by extension to some total order consistent with program order and read-from constraints. The spec initializes empty operation queues, allows issuing requests, responding to reads and writes, and internal steps that only extend the order relation, and it verifies the system with a temporal specification using weak fairness for response actions and for internal ordering steps that eventually compare distinct operations.
IfThenElse: IF opIdQ(oi).source = InitWr THEN InitMem[opIdQ(oi).req.adr] ELSE opIdQ(opIdQ(oi).source).req.val
IF src = InitWr THEN InitMem[req.adr] ELSE opIdQ(src).req.val
FunctionConstructor:
[req    |-> [req EXCEPT !.val = val],
                             reg    |-> Done,
                             source |-> src  ]
FunctionOverride:
[opQ EXCEPT ![proc][idx] = 
                            [req    |-> [req EXCEPT !.val = val],
                             reg    |-> Done,
                             source |-> src  ]]
RecordConstructor:
[req    |-> [req EXCEPT !.val = val],
                             reg    |-> Done,
                             source |-> src  ]
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE v : v \notin [proc : Proc, idx : Nat]
CHOOSE i \in DOMAIN opQ[proc] : opQ[proc][i].reg = reg
TemporalSubscript:
WF_<<regFile, opQ, opOrder>>(RespondToWr(proc, reg) 
                                        \/ RespondToRd(proc, reg) )

WF_<<regFile, opQ, opOrder>>(
                   /\ (oi \in opId) /\ (oj \in opId)
                   /\ Internal

DivisionNotes: InitWr is classified under Init because the rule states any operator whose name is exactly "Init" or begins with "Init" belongs in OperatorDefNames_Init, even though InitWr is a CHOOSE-defined value rather than an initialization predicate.
Serializable is classified as a StatePredicate because it is Boolean-valued, contains no primed variables, and contains no temporal operators; it is a state property rather than an action.
Done, totalOpOrder, and other helper operators were placed in ValueDef by elimination because they are non-action and non-temporal, and are not Init-prefixed Boolean state predicates.
